dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY
dialogueInline.text: Before the Crossing

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Distance used to be a fact of life. Then, for a long time, it became the fact that determined nearly everything else.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Humanity had spread among the stars along a network of engineered passages known as the corridors. A ship entering one of these carefully measured volumes could travel at speeds impossible in ordinary space. Journeys that should have consumed lifetimes became possible within a human life.

title: The Connected Age (Pre-Fleet)
summary: The connected age — a single civilian transit arrival anchors a prosperous, pre-Fleet civilization built on engineered corridors.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The corridors were not shortcuts granted by a generous universe. Their passage depended on reciprocal fields, precise timing, stable reference points, and the skill of people who could tell a safe crossing from one that only appeared safe. Keeping the network open was work. So was keeping the ships that used it alive.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: During the long connected age, worlds came to depend upon that work. People, crops, knowledge, and materials passed between settlements that would otherwise have grown old without ever speaking. This was before Fleet. The network was already a civilization's lifeline.

Light and atmosphere: Radiant gold, turquoise and rose daylight, with soft memory-like vignetting.

title: The Shattering
summary: The Shattering — one intelligible passage failure reveals the severing of trade, communication and rescue.
settingText: HISTORICAL PROLOGUE — THE SHATTERING — CORRIDOR FAILURE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Then came the Shattering.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Reliable fast travel failed across the settled regions. Places that had depended upon one another found themselves separated by journeys that could take months or years. Some routes remained possible at punishing cost. Others were damaged, lost, or too uncertain to trust.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: News arrived late. A shipment might reach a settlement after the people who ordered it had moved, died, or learned to live without it. An emergency in one system could become a historical footnote before anyone capable of helping even heard about it.

The reader sees a broken connection, not a crowded battle or explosion montage. Light and atmosphere: Cool teal and bruised blue with one restrained hot interruption; faint historic haze at page edges.

title: The Core — Reach and Resolve
summary: Core infrastructure survived unevenly; Fleet protects working corridors, while officials make painful triage decisions about those beyond reach.
settingText: HISTORICAL PROLOGUE — POST-SHATTERING — CORE TRANSIT AND RELIEF HUB

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Life went on because it had to. But what survived the Shattering was not shared equally.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Core retained much of the old network’s machinery, knowledge, and military strength. Its functioning ports and repair yards could still provision ships, preserve navigation records, and defend the routes within reach.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Fleet emerged after the Shattering around two obligations: Reach, to find the way back to people; and Resolve, to help them endure when the way was gone. The service was real. So were the limits. Each protected departure meant a decision about which distant settlement would have to wait.

panelPlan: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ILLUSTRATION. In a mature, functioning Core transit and relief hub, a civilian logistics coordinator and Fleet officer confront an actual dispatch choice at a physical loading gantry. In the same coherent view, a maintained relief transport is actively being loaded with food and medical containers while a second, equally prepared consignment remains behind at an unused departure berth. Fleet is disciplined navy/white/gold, and the hub has inherited industrial capacity, intact equipment, and expert workers. The human decision about limited reach is the focal point, never a triumphant Fleet beauty shot. Warm daylight on substantial infrastructure, cool navy in the working shadows; restrained historical vignette.

title: The Verge — Networks of Necessity
summary: Verge farmers and civilian port crews sustain trade and mutual aid with capable local institutions but little reserve capacity.
settingText: HISTORICAL PROLOGUE — POST-SHATTERING — VERGE AGRICULTURAL FREEPORT

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Beyond the Core’s protected routes, the Verge did not stop working. Farms, ports, and local governments made their own arrangements for moving food, repairing ships, and keeping neighboring settlements supplied.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Their strength was cooperation built close to home: shared storage, independent pilots, local protection, and bargains made face to face. A working departure might depend on a farmer's harvest, a mechanic's last spare part, and a broker who knew which passage could still be trusted.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They had skill and thriving communities, but not the Core’s inherited reserves. When a ship failed or a crossing closed, the loss fell immediately upon people who had no second shipment waiting.

panelPlan: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ILLUSTRATION. A functioning Verge grain freeport in broad agricultural daylight. A specific farmer and civilian cargo coordinator check a repaired compact freighter's last loading cradle while crew members transfer grain containers from a well-kept communal granary. A small group of ordinary people wait with goods for passage; a single empty reserve bay makes fragility clear without grime or deprivation. Practical tan and muted green textiles, route markings rendered only graphically, honest repair work, nearby fields and well-run civilian infrastructure. The focal action is cooperative logistics that visibly supports livelihoods, and the scarce backup capacity is readable. Amber, muted green, cool daylight; gentle historical vignette.

title: The Shards — Industry from Ruin
summary: Shard communities rebuild industrial capacity with skilled labor under chronic shortages; armed captains emerge from uneven access and contested trade.
settingText: HISTORICAL PROLOGUE — POST-SHATTERING — SHARD INDUSTRIAL REPAIR BERTH

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: In the Shards, the collapse left wreckage, interrupted supply, and machines too valuable to abandon. People made communities around the work of recovery: salvaging structures, restoring equipment, and keeping difficult ships serviceable.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Repair crews could turn a failed hull into transport and a dismantled station into an industry. But chronic shortages shaped every calculation. A needed component might be available only through a dangerous route, a costly bargain, or traffic unwilling to share.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Some captains began taking what trade would not provide. Others defended their neighbors, carried supplies, or tried to keep violence away from the docks. Across the divided regions, knowing a route was not the same as having the means to use it. The Shattering had made security, technology, food, and opportunity profoundly unequal.

panelPlan: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ILLUSTRATION. A sophisticated Shard civilian repair berth within a repurposed industrial framework. Foreground Shard engineer and civilian dock steward work side by side to bring a patched, clearly practical transport back into service. A finite rack of salvage components and an unfinished adjacent hull show supply shortages; distant small craft and capable repair crews convey functioning industry and defended routes without a raid or battle. Pale gray and gray-white working layers, dark functional underlayers, bright-red marks, visibly repaired structures; precise, plausible ship geometry and orderly active equipment. Main visual beat: skilled recovery under material scarcity, with a difficult choice over a last critical component. Cool mineral light and restrained red accents, softened historic edges.

title: The Route Is Open Again
summary: Routes reopen — one family approaches a civilian grain freighter; the prologue gives way to Issue 1 with hope and unresolved inequality, without spoiling the crossing.
settingText: LUMINARA FIELDS — CIVILIAN GRAIN FREIGHT DOCK — PRESENT DAY

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now the corridors are beginning to reopen.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A route that once consumed a generation's patience can again become a practical journey. For a family, a new home. For a farmer, a market that might keep the next crop growing. For a settlement short of food, the sight of a freighter on approach. For Fleet, a chance to restore a service it believes civilization needs.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: But faster travel does not erase what separation cost. Governments and borders have changed, as have the resources and power each community brings to the crossing. People remember whom they could depend on and whom they could not. The corridors remain demanding: a failed timing reference, a missed window, or debris in the lane can still kill. And someone must decide which ship goes first and who will protect it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: On Luminara, cargo crews are securing grain for the crossing. A mother and her son carry their belongings aboard, hoping there is a better place to live at the other end.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The route is open again.

The passengers survived, but Auric received less food than it had counted on.

dialogueInline.text: The stolen grain did not vanish into somebody's private fortune. It reached hungry households at Black Drift. Abby Saville, Tessa Banks, and Billie Rusk know exactly what the supplies mean to those families. They disagree about what continued raiding will do to the merchants they need to keep sailing. Meanwhile, route broker Jex Marrin knows more about the interception than the people who suffered it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION

The faster route promises prosperity, but arriving families are already finding the celebrated freeport crowded and short of heat.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The evacuation freighter Mercy of Dawn came to Auric under attack, carrying Verge and Shard families who needed a safe berth more urgently than they needed permission to approach one. Commodore Ella Venn abandoned her assigned supply screen to answer their distress. The decision saved people and put Auric's heating and medical supplies at risk. She later refused a Fleet detention order that would have separated patients from their caregivers.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The rescue was hardly the work of one uniform. Naomi Sol led civilian contact. Richard Secundo and his son Paul kept people alive aboard a ship coming apart. Tessa Banks helped protect passengers from raiders wearing her own faction's colors. Abby Saville opposed Billie's use of civilians as leverage, and independent Shard captains began making different choices about whom they would follow.

Heat and medicine remain scarce. Families who lived there before the refugee arrivals have claims as real as the claims of those who fled.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Dr. Richard Secundo has made public the original records from Tal Corvus. Some of the shortages imposed on Shard districts were not mechanical failures or unavoidable consequences of isolation: supplies were deliberately diverted after political protests. The evidence spread despite an attempt to silence him. Its publication has strained the authority of the Silent Triarch and divided people who once fought alongside one another.

Jex Marrin helped open hidden approaches for evacuees; his sister Tali has since disappeared from contact, and he does not know whether she escaped.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tal Corvus's evacuation passed through a corridor that everyone knew would be contested. The plan nearly failed when armed ships pressed the departure lane and two civilian tugs drifted out of safe formation.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tessa Banks held Gravefire at the departure mouth, damaging the ship's already vulnerable cooling systems while guiding the final craft through. Naomi Sol used warning from Jex Marrin to keep another hostile screen from isolating the convoy. Oren Pike abandoned his carefully staged position long enough to recover a stranded tug. A junior Fleet escort officer left formation without permission to reach another; Thunderbreak's commander, Erin Deka, chose to cover the gap that officer opened. Those were two decisions by two different officers, and Fleet is keeping a record of both.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The families reached safety. Their arrival did not replenish Auric's stores, repair Gravefire, or settle the competing explanations each faction offered for the rescue. Nor did it erase the pressure on Billie Rusk, whose refusal to destroy independent Shard food production has complicated her position with the Triarch.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Off her former bridge, Ella Venn has begun discovering that an old acquaintance may answer her calls without being free to act on them. She cannot relieve Deka of responsibility, and she cannot promise Auric help the Fleet has not authorized.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The rescue brought people through. Feeding them will require another crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: In Veil Market, people have been learning what a route is worth when a ration door is shut. Jex Marrin, who once earned his living selling privileged crossing information, opened a verified public timing bulletin so civilian pilots could find the next safe passage. It helped freighters move. It also gave raiders the same information.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Billie Rusk, short of fuel and supply after defying the Triarch, attacked a Verge relief shipment. Twenty-eight of the promised hundred crates were lost. Seventy-two reached Auric, where the arithmetic became smaller portions on actual plates. Gravefire, still damaged from Tal Corvus, placed itself between Billie's guns and the freighter. Billie withdrew rather than fire through Tess Banks's ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Deka kept Thunderbreak's limited defensive protection available without taking command of the Shard escort. Abby restricted the intelligence shared with Billie's crew, though she could not issue orders to that independent captain. The convoy that followed showed how much work cooperation required even when nobody fired.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Meanwhile, copies of Jex's route information have begun moving through working crews faster than any single authority can suppress them. The Triarch has noticed. So has Venn, who is learning to secure voluntary technical help rather than issue orders she no longer has the right to give.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The next crossings will carry both food and medicine. Someone has decided they should not be allowed through.

dialogueInline.text: Seven Decisions

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At Auric Gate, the Silent Triarch attempted to stop civilian traffic by placing Shard pickets across the available crossing windows. Auric had supplies waiting on the other side and two brief openings, half an hour apart. Naomi Sol led the exposed food convoy through the first. Tessa Banks brought medical freight toward the second.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The blockade did not end because one commander won a battle. Abby Saville sent a dangerous message to captains whose crews had their own loyalties and families. Seven of them independently turned their weapons away from the civilian lane. Billie Rusk used Ashfang to shield Gravefire from a loyalist attack without joining Abby's rebellion. Deka held Thunderbreak's defensive overlap and refused to let Fleet claim credit for the captains' decisions. Food came through with damage to one freighter; the medical crossing survived without a firefight.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Those decisions have consequences inside the Shards, where obedience and standing cannot be replaced by a single public statement. Around Tal Corvus, crews have also observed an unfamiliar physical disturbance in the built environment, with no reliable explanation for it yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Venn's influence beyond the chain of command has grown, but she has not recovered Thunderbreak. The coming problems will test whether cooperation can be built around evidence instead of authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For the first time in a while, the danger ahead may not be an enemy ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Calm Corridor appeared stable by every ordinary measurement. Then a survey ship saw a second image of itself, following its actual maneuver after a measurable delay. The anomaly was real enough to endanger navigation, but neither the instruments nor the physicists could yet explain it completely.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Jia Morgan found that the delayed returns grew more dangerous when ships fired their maneuvering systems in unison. Formation guidance began treating the echoes as real hulls while actual civilian vessels lost safe separation. Naomi Sol broke the synchronized pattern with staggered manual instructions. Tess Banks kept Gravefire and its passengers on the real course rather than chasing an image of her own ship. The convoy came through because different captains trusted a shared measurement without making identical movements.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Fear Mask used frightening recordings to pronounce certainty where researchers could only report observations. The attempt to turn uncertainty into obedience met witnesses who had seen the crossing for themselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: But the Shards have other ways of contesting authority. Abby Saville's independent captains have already challenged what the Triarch can demand of them, and Tess's standing carries weight beyond her own vessel. Their problems at home have not disappeared while the corridor has been misbehaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At Shardfall, Oren Pike challenged Tessa Banks before witnesses, turning the shortages and unfinished repair debts of the Shards into an argument about who deserved to lead. Pike proved that he could fight. Tess won, with a real injury to her left forearm, and then refused to kill him. The outcome changed what the witnesses were willing to say in public. It did not change how much food was available.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Two more Shard captains withdrew from the Raid Mask's muster. The Triarch responded by freezing their berths, placing costs on crews who had made their own political choices. Abby Saville must live with the consequences of offering those captains an alternative she cannot guarantee will be easy.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: While the challenge drew attention, Naomi Sol found a safer way to move an overcrowded ration line through Veil Market. Jex Marrin and the market workers are still dealing with diverted supplies, incomplete deliveries, and the difference between food that exists on a ledger and food a family can actually reach.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A watched duel can end in an instant. A hungry market cannot.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Someone tried to kill Jex Marrin while Veil Market was already close to breaking under real shortages. The attempt helped provoke panic, a fire, and a struggle over stored food. Jex survived, injured, and opened reserves that had once been part of his private commercial advantage. When the fire threatened the passage used by rescuers, he surrendered more access and allowed workers to cut through goods he had expected to sell.

title: Previously in Rex Fleet — What the Ledger Cost
summary: Editorial introduction / recap from Season One Writing v8. Preserve all caption text exactly, in order.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That decision saved routes for food and medicine. It also left honest buyers without purchases they had already paid for. Jex's records began linking the attacker, paid agitators, and diverted cargo, but those connections do not mean all of Veil Market's hunger was manufactured. Naomi Sol followed the evidence without confusing sabotage with scarcity itself. Venn and Sera Dain helped obtain medical access without handing Fleet an invitation to occupy the market.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Jex has released enough of his transactions for others to verify the pattern while holding back private refuge routes that might still matter to his missing sister, Tali. Copies are beyond his control now.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: What happens next will depend on what those payments purchased—and on the people who have to live with the answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The emergency at Shatterforge began with equipment that should have protected its people. Industrial service vents were deliberately locked, forcing families toward departures that could be controlled. Tess Banks reached the manual relief system. Abby Saville brought Scythe of Saville over the exhaust, using her ship's shields to keep the discharge away from occupied terraces while the evacuation proceeded.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The last skiffs took longer than the shield system could safely promise. Venn, directing Fleet resources, chose to protect the final civilian craft rather than draw that protection toward Abby's increasingly exposed ship. Scythe stayed over the vent. After the last craft cleared, the ship vanished behind the furnace bloom, its fate unconfirmed. Tess got the rescued people docked before turning to the question she could hardly bear to ask.

dialogueInline.text: A Road Still Open

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric Gate was carrying civilians before the fleets began fighting over it. Fleet, Verge, and independent Shard ships faced one another across a passage none could afford to lose. Pike sought a battle the cameras would remember. Venn declined a shot that would have put civilians behind the target at risk. Naomi, Halev, and Tess kept traffic moving even as the formation broke apart.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Then the Gate's physical readings began to echo the battle. Jia Morgan found that synchronized weapons fire was coupling to the same anomalous returns previously measured in the Calm Corridor. The harder the ships fought in step, the less reliable their picture of the real traffic became. Stopping synchronized volleys was a technical necessity, not a sudden end to the fighting.

title: Previously in Rex Fleet — A Road Still Open
summary: Editorial introduction / recap from Season One Writing v8. Preserve all caption text exactly, in order.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Abby Saville returned aboard a damaged Scythe with survivors and captains who had chosen her. She directed them toward the civilian lane. After Verge escorts relinquished their offensive locks, Venn asked Thunderbreak to power down its offensive batteries and cover civilians. Deka, still commanding the cruiser and responsible for its exposed flank, made the ship-handling decision. Other captains chose their own restraint. Billie Rusk prevented Pike from turning the remaining confusion into a massacre.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The firing stopped. The echoes diminished. The road remained open, scarred and difficult, for the ships that had waited through the battle.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: No faction surrendered its principles, command, or claim to have acted correctly. The next civilian convoy still needs an agreed time to cross.
